quote: (a) Kubient agrees to indemnify, defend, and hold harmless Customer and its officers, directors, managers, members, agents, and employees from all third-party allegations, claims, actions, losses, expenses, damages, costs (including, without limitation, reasonable attorneys' fees) or liabilities ("Claims") arising out of or in connection with:
rationale: Section 10(a) gives us a broad Kubient-side defence and indemnity for third-party Claims arising out of the Services, the Auction Platform, the Creative served by the Auction Platform, Kubient's breach of any representation or warranty, and the acts or omissions of Kubient and its subcontractors. IP infringement is squarely covered: Kubient warrants in §9(b)(i) that the Service and deliverables do not infringe or misappropriate any third-party IP, privacy or publicity rights, and 10(a)(iv) indemnifies breach of that warranty, in addition to the general "arising out of the Services / Auction Platform" trigger. Vendor misconduct is covered by 10(a)(v). Section 11 supplies standard procedure (prompt notice that is not a condition to recovery, indemnifying-party control with no liability-admitting settlement absent our consent, cooperation at the indemnifying party's cost), and §7(a) carves indemnification out of the consequential-damages exclusion; there is no monetary liability cap applied to the indemnity, so no super-cap concern arises. This meets the preferred position. Noted but not flagged: AP's reciprocal indemnity in 10(b) is somewhat wider than the preferred "Customer content and Customer's breach of law" formulation (it also picks up AP's breach of any representation or warranty and acts/omissions of AP and its contractors), and the Creative limb of Kubient's indemnity is knowledge-qualified. These are mirror-image, minor sub-elements against an otherwise strong vendor indemnity and do not warrant a redline.

proposal.comment: [Playbook] The Agreement has no ownership article, so we have added one: we retain all right, title and interest in our Content, Properties and Customer Data, Kubient keeps its Auction Platform and pre-existing tools, and any deliverables created for us are assigned with a licence-back for embedded Kubient IP. We have also confirmed Kubient may use Customer Data only to provide the Services, with no joint ownership and no right to monetise our audience data.

ops.text: Ownership. As between the Parties, Customer exclusively owns and retains all right, title and interest in and to the Content, the Properties, the Inventory, the Requests and all data and information generated by, collected from or relating to the Properties, visitors to the Properties or Customer's audience or database (collectively, "Customer Data"), together with all intellectual property rights therein. Kubient exclusively owns and retains all right, title and interest in and to the Auction Platform and its pre-existing technology, tools and know-how, including generic improvements thereto. Kubient hereby assigns to Customer all right, title and interest in and to any deliverables, reports, work product or other materials created for Customer under this Agreement (excluding Kubient's pre-existing technology, tools and know-how), and grants Customer a perpetual, irrevocable, worldwide, royalty-free license to use, modify and sublicense any Kubient intellectual property embedded in such deliverables for Customer's business purposes. Kubient may access and use Customer Data solely to provide the Services to Customer, and shall not sell, license or otherwise monetize Customer Data. Nothing in this Agreement creates any joint ownership of, or transfers to Kubient any ownership interest in, the Content, the Properties, Customer Data or any other Customer intellectual property.

proposal.summary: Insert an ownership clause: AP retains all rights in Content, Properties and Customer Data; Kubient keeps its platform but assigns deliverables and grants a licence-back; no joint ownership or data monetisation.

quote: (viii) it is the rightful owner or licensee of all intellectual property rights to the Service, the Auction Platform and products delivered hereunder;
rationale: The Agreement contains no intellectual property / ownership article. Nothing states that AP retains ownership of its Content, Properties or the audience/visitor data and Requests flowing through the Auction Platform, and there is no assignment of, or licence back to, deliverables. The only ownership-adjacent language runs the other way or is too narrow: Kubient warrants at p0040 that it owns "the Service, the Auction Platform and products delivered hereunder" (i.e. deliverables) while AP's only licence (p0002) is limited, non-transferable, non-sublicensable and revocable; p0025 makes AP liable for the Content without confirming ownership; and p0065 covers only names, trademarks and logos. Kubient's use of visitor data is addressed only as a security warranty (p0035), with no purpose limitation or bar on monetisation — a material gap for AP audience data. This fails both the preferred and fallback positions, so we have inserted a minimal ownership clause: AP retains all rights in Content, Properties and Customer Data; Kubient keeps its platform and pre-existing tools; deliverables are assigned with a perpetual, royalty-free licence back for embedded Kubient IP; no joint ownership and no data monetisation.
ruleTitle: Ownership of deliverables and Customer Data

proposal.comment: [Playbook] We have added a mutual cap on liability at the greater of twelve (12) months' amounts paid or payable between the Parties and USD 1,000,000, since Section 7 currently excludes consequential damages but leaves both Parties' direct liability entirely uncapped; the fixed floor is needed because Customer pays no fees under the revenue-share model. Indemnification, confidentiality, data protection and security, gross negligence, wilful misconduct, fraud and infringement of the other Party's IP sit outside the cap, consistent with the carve-outs already in Section 7(a).

ops.text: (b) Except with respect to Excluded Claims, each Party's total aggregate liability arising out of or relating to this Agreement shall not exceed the greater of (i) the aggregate amounts paid or payable between the Parties under this Agreement in the twelve (12) months immediately preceding the event giving rise to the claim and (ii) USD 1,000,000. "Excluded Claims" means a Party's breach of its confidentiality, data protection or security obligations, its indemnification obligations, its gross negligence, wilful misconduct or fraud, and its infringement of the other Party's intellectual property rights, none of which shall be subject to the foregoing limitation.

proposal.summary: Add a mutual liability cap (greater of 12 months' amounts paid/payable and USD 1,000,000) with uncapped Excluded Claims to Section 7.

quote: (a) EXCEPT WITH RESPECT TO THE PARTIES' LIABILITY FOR INDEMNIFICATION, OR LIABILITY FOR BREACH OF CONFIDENTIALITY, NEITHER PARTY SHALL BE LIABLE FOR ANY CONSEQUENTIAL, INCIDENTAL, INDIRECT, PUNITIVE, SPECIAL OR OTHER SIMILAR DAMAGES
rationale: Section 7 is the only limitation-of-liability provision and contains solely a mutual exclusion of consequential/indirect damages (with carve-outs for indemnification and confidentiality). No monetary cap exists anywhere in the Agreement: searches for "exceed" and "aggregate" return no cap language, and the indemnity (§10) and warranty (§9) provisions contain none. Both Parties' direct liability is therefore unlimited, which fails even the fallback position (mutual cap of 12 months' fees). The revenue-share payment structure in §5 (Kubient pays Customer a share of revenue; Customer pays no fees) means a fees-based cap alone would be illusory, so we add the USD 1,000,000 floor from the preferred position and keep indemnification, confidentiality/data protection, gross negligence, wilful misconduct, fraud and IP infringement uncapped as Excluded Claims, mirroring the carve-outs already in §7(a).
ruleTitle: Limitation of liability — cap, mutuality and carve-outs

quote: (h) Neither Party may assign (voluntarily, by operation of law, or otherwise) this Agreement or any rights or obligations under this Agreement without the other Party's prior written consent, which shall not be unreasonably withheld, provided however, that either Party may assign this Agreement without approval or consent to any affiliate or purchaser of all or substantially all of said Party's assets related to the subject matter of this Agreement or to any successor by way of merger, stock sale, consolidation or similar transaction.
rationale: Paragraph (h) gives AP exactly what the preferred position requires on the material terms: AP may assign without consent to an affiliate, to a purchaser of all or substantially all relevant assets, or to a successor by merger, stock sale or consolidation, and any other assignment requires consent that may not be unreasonably withheld. There is no walk-away feature — no blanket prohibition on Customer assignment, and no deemed-assignment or change-of-control provision anywhere in the document (search for "change of control" returns nothing). The termination provision (p0016) is limited to expiry-of-term notice, material breach and insolvency, so Kubient has no right to terminate or re-price on an AP change of control. Two sub-elements fall short of the ideal preferred wording and are noted rather than flagged: the free-assignment carve-out is mutual (so Kubient may also assign to its own affiliate or acquirer without our consent, which is squarely the fallback position of a mutual right to assign to successors), and there is no express bar on Kubient assigning to an AP competitor. Neither is material enough to redline given the clause otherwise sits at or above the fallback.

quote: Nothing herein is intended nor shall be construed as creating an exclusive arrangement between Customer and Kubient. This Agreement will not restrict Customer offering Inventory via other agents or otherwise selling Inventory to any third parties.
rationale: The Services clause expressly disclaims any exclusive arrangement and confirms we remain free to offer or sell Inventory through other agents or third parties, which meets the preferred position (no exclusivity or sole-supplier obligation on the Customer). A full-text sweep for "exclusive", "sole", and third-party restriction language found no other provision binding our supply freedom: the remaining "exclusive" references concern a non-exclusive license granted to us, exclusive jurisdiction, each party's own trademark ownership, and the no-third-party-beneficiary clause — none of which restrict our procurement. No redline required.

quote: Except for termination for material breach as detailed in paragraph 4(b), Kubient shall be entitled to all fees generated during the termination period regardless of which Party terminates the Agreement,
rationale: The Agreement contains no liquidated damages, penalty, minimum-fee, or early-termination-fee obligation payable by AP, meeting the preferred position of no Customer-payable liquidated damages. Searches for "liquidated damages", "penalt", and "termination fee" return nothing, and a full read of the single section confirms it. The only money-on-termination language (para 4(a)) simply confirms Kubient keeps revenue-share fees actually generated during the 90-day notice period — that is earned compensation under the revenue-share in Section 5, not a liquidated sum or exit penalty, and it does not apply where AP terminates for Kubient's material breach. Termination consequences in 4(c) are limited to ceasing Services, revoking the license, and returning Confidential Information, with no payment trigger. Note also that Section 7 excludes punitive and special damages for both Parties, further reducing any penalty exposure. No redline is warranted.
ruleTitle: Liquidated damages and penalties payable by Customer

proposal.comment: [Playbook] We have extended the licence to our affiliates and to contractors acting on our behalf (with a matching carve-out to the third-party access restriction), and made the licence revocable only on expiration or termination, since our playbook does not accept a licence that Kubient can revoke at will or that excludes the affiliates and vendors who actually operate our properties. If helpful, we can instead cover affiliates on written notice to Kubient.

ops.newText: Kubient hereby grants to Customer and its affiliates, and to contractors acting on Customer's behalf, a limited, royalty-free, non-exclusive, non-transferable and non-assignable (except as expressly permitted under this Agreement), without right of sublicense, license, revocable only upon expiration or termination of this Agreement, to access, participate in and use to the full extent the Auction Platform as hosted by Kubient,
ops.oldText: Kubient hereby grants to Customer a limited, royalty-free, non-exclusive, non-transferable, non-assignable, without right of sublicense, revocable license to access, participate in and use to the full extent the Auction Platform as hosted by Kubient,

ops.newText: allow third-party access to the Service (other than access by Customer's affiliates and by contractors acting on Customer's behalf, for whose compliance with this Agreement Customer remains responsible).
ops.oldText: allow third-party access to the Service.

proposal.summary: Extend the Auction Platform licence to AP affiliates and contractors acting on AP's behalf and remove Kubient's at-will revocation right

quote: Kubient hereby grants to Customer a limited, royalty-free, non-exclusive, non-transferable, non-assignable, without right of sublicense, revocable license to access, participate in and use to the full extent the Auction Platform as hosted by Kubient,
rationale: The Auction Platform grant in paragraph 2 is expressly "revocable" with no limitation to a termination event, which lets Kubient pull the licence at its discretion — walk-away territory under this rule. It also runs to "Customer" only: affiliates and contractors are not named, and paragraph 5(a) affirmatively bars third-party access to the Service absent Kubient's advance written approval, so there is no notice-based path to add affiliates as the fallback requires. Assignment is not the problem — paragraph 12(h) already permits assignment without consent to an affiliate, an asset purchaser or a successor by merger, so the successor-transfer element of the fallback is met. Because the revocability and affiliate/contractor exclusion both fail the fallback, we take the grant to the preferred position: licence extended to AP affiliates and contractors acting on AP's behalf (with a matching carve-out in paragraph 5(a) and AP remaining responsible for their compliance) and revocable only on expiration or termination, which is consistent with paragraph 4(c)(ii) revoking the licence at termination.

quote: Nothing herein is intended nor shall be construed as creating an exclusive arrangement between Customer and Kubient. This Agreement will not restrict Customer offering Inventory via other agents or otherwise selling Inventory to any third parties.
rationale: The Agreement contains no non-compete, exclusivity or field-of-use restriction binding us. Section 1 (p0001) does the opposite of the risk this rule targets: it expressly disclaims any exclusive arrangement and confirms the Agreement will not restrict Customer from offering Inventory via other agents or selling Inventory to third parties. Searches for "compet", "exclusiv", "restrict", "solicit", "shall not" and "Customer will not" surfaced no covenant limiting our business lines, products or territory. The only Customer-side prohibitions are the standard software-license protections in Section 6(a) (p0025) — no transfer or third-party access, no modification/derivative works, no reverse engineering, no resale or service-bureau use of the Service. Those protect Kubient's IP in its own platform and are not field-of-use or competing-activity restrictions, so they are not flagged here. The clause meets the preferred position (no non-compete on Customer); no redline required.

quote: Neither Party may terminate this Agreement during the Initial Term except as set forth in paragraph 4(b) or any Exhibit. Either Party may terminate this Agreement for any reason following the Initial Term upon ninety (90) days written notice to the other Party. Except for termination for material breach as detailed in paragraph 4(b), Kubient shall be entitled to all fees generated during the termination period regardless of which Party terminates the Agreement
rationale: Paragraph 4(a) sits at the playbook fallback and is therefore acceptable without redline. (1) The Initial Term is only one (1) year, so the absence of a mid-term convenience right does not trigger the "term longer than 12 months" / multi-year walk-away test; thereafter AP may terminate for any reason on ninety (90) days' notice, within the fallback's 60–90 day band. (2) There is no early-termination fee or penalty on AP — Kubient is only entitled to fees generated during the 90-day notice period, i.e. revenue actually earned while it is still performing, not a termination charge; and because fees are a revenue share paid by Kubient to AP (para. 5), there are no prepaid fees requiring a pro-rata refund. (3) Kubient's convenience right is symmetrical and requires the full ninety (90) days' notice, so it is not in walk-away territory (which is vendor notice of fewer than 90 days). Sub-elements short of the preferred position, noted but not flagged: AP has no 30-day convenience right during the Initial Term, and Kubient's post-Initial-Term convenience right is not confined to the end of a renewal term, so Kubient could exit mid-renewal-year on 90 days' notice. If this agreement is later extended to a multi-year committed term or an Exhibit adds AP-side fees, we should revisit and add a 30-day AP convenience right with a pro-rata refund and strip Kubient's mid-term exit.

quote: Customer agrees to provide all reasonable and necessary access, support and cooperation for Kubient to provide the Services in a timely and effective manner.
rationale: Searches for "audit", "inspect" and "records" return nothing, and a full read of the agreement (the entire document is a single section) confirms Kubient is given no right to audit, inspect, verify or access AP's books, records or systems. The only access-related obligation on AP is the cooperation/access language in Section 1 (p0001), which is limited to enabling delivery of the Services and is not a verification or audit right; likewise, Impressions being "measured by Kubient" (p0009) is a metering mechanic, not an audit of our usage. Because no vendor-side audit right binds us, there is nothing that could exceed the preferred limits on frequency, notice, cost or system access — the position is better for us than the playbook preferred, so no redline is warranted. Worth noting for the business team only: AP correspondingly has no express contractual right to audit Kubient's Impression measurement or revenue-share reporting; that is a separate reporting/verification point outside this rule's scope and could be raised if revenue assurance is a concern.

quote: (a) This Agreement is governed in all respects by the laws of the State of Delaware without giving effect to its conflict of laws principles. Each Party hereby irrevocably submits for all disputes to the exclusive jurisdiction and venue of the state and federal courts located in New York, New York.
rationale: Section 14(a) selects Delaware law with exclusive jurisdiction and venue in the state and federal courts in New York, New York. Delaware law sits squarely at the playbook fallback, and the forum is in fact our preferred venue (New York County courts), so the clause meets the rule on its material terms and is not redlined. Two points noted but not flagged: (i) the ideal outcome would be New York substantive law to match the New York forum, a wording-level improvement only; and (ii) Section 8 (p0028) also provides for AAA Commercial Rules arbitration, which sits in tension with the exclusive-court submission in 14(a). That arbitration is administered domestically under AAA rules with no foreign seat, so it does not reach the walk-away trigger (mandatory arbitration seated abroad); the internal inconsistency between the two provisions is better addressed under the dispute-resolution rule than duplicated here.

quote: Nothing herein is intended nor shall be construed as creating an exclusive arrangement between Customer and Kubient. This Agreement will not restrict Customer offering Inventory via other agents or otherwise selling Inventory to any third parties.
rationale: The Agreement contains no most-favoured-nation or price/terms-parity obligation in either direction. I read the entire document (single section, paragraphs p0000–p0074) and searched for "most favored nation", "no less favorable", "favourable", "third party terms" and "best" — no clause requires AP to extend to Kubient any pricing, revenue share or other terms it grants to third parties, and nothing requires AP to match third-party offers. Section 5 (p0023) leaves revenue sharing to individual Exhibits without any parity undertaking, and Section 1 (p0001) expressly confirms the arrangement is non-exclusive and does not restrict AP from offering Inventory through other agents or selling Inventory to third parties — language that benefits us and is the opposite of an MFN burden. This meets the preferred position (no MFN obligation on Customer), so no redline is warranted. Note for diligence only: the fee Exhibits are not part of this document, so if any Exhibit or order form later introduces a parity or rate-matching covenant running in Kubient's favour, it should be reviewed against this rule.

quote: Nothing herein is intended nor shall be construed as creating an exclusive arrangement between Customer and Kubient. This Agreement will not restrict Customer offering Inventory via other agents or otherwise selling Inventory to any third parties.
rationale: The Agreement imposes no minimum purchase commitment, minimum spend, minimum impression/volume obligation or take-or-pay on AP. Section 5 (Fees and Payment, p0023) is a pure revenue-share: Kubient contracts with Advertisers and remits AP's share within seven days of receipt, with no fees payable by AP other than applicable transaction taxes. Section 1 (p0001) expressly disclaims exclusivity and confirms AP may offer or sell Inventory through other agents or third parties, so there is no volume cap or channel restriction on us either. The only "minimum" references are the Customer-set floor price in the "Winning Bid Price" definition (p0014), which benefits AP, and Kubient's disclaimer of any guaranteed minimum revenue (p0062) — neither is a commitment binding AP. This meets the preferred position (no minimum commitment; consideration flows from actual monetized usage). Noted but not flagged under this rule: the Initial Term is one year with no convenience termination during that period, and Kubient retains fees generated during a termination notice period (p0016) — a term/termination point rather than a purchase commitment, since no spend obligation attaches.
ruleTitle: Minimum purchase commitments and volume restrictions on Customer

quote: (c) The relationship of the Parties is that of independent contractors, and nothing herein is intended, nor should be construed, to create a partnership, agency, joint venture or employment relationship.
rationale: Searches for "solicit", "induce", "recruit", "hire" and "employ" return no restrictive covenant; the only employment-related language is the independent contractor clause (p0066), the confidentiality permission to share with employees/directors (p0061), and the indemnity references to employees/hired third parties (p0047, p0051-p0052). The miscellaneous block (p0064-p0073) contains no non-solicitation or no-hire provision. The agreement therefore imposes no non-solicit on AP, which is the playbook's preferred position, so nothing to redline.

proposal.comment: [Playbook] We have shortened the post-Initial Term notice period from 90 to 30 days and confirmed it covers non-renewal, since our playbook requires auto-renewing terms to be exitable on 30 days' notice (60 days at the outside). We are happy to land at 60 days if that is easier for you.

ops.newText: Either Party may terminate this Agreement or elect not to renew any renewal term for any reason following the Initial Term upon thirty (30) days written notice to the other Party.
ops.oldText: Either Party may terminate this Agreement for any reason following the Initial Term upon ninety (90) days written notice to the other Party.

proposal.summary: Reduce non-renewal/termination notice window after Initial Term from 90 days to 30 days.

quote: This Agreement will automatically renew for additional 1-year terms unless earlier terminated pursuant to this Agreement's express provisions (together with the Initial Term, such additional periods the "Term"). Neither Party may terminate this Agreement during the Initial Term except as set forth in paragraph 4(b) or any Exhibit. Either Party may terminate this Agreement for any reason following the Initial Term upon ninety (90) days written notice to the other Party.
rationale: The Agreement auto-renews for successive 1-year terms (renewal length is acceptable and not multi-year), but the only route out after the Initial Term is convenience termination on ninety (90) days' written notice. That is the effective non-renewal window, and it exceeds the fallback ceiling of 60 days, so the clause fails the fallback on a material term (it is at, not beyond, the walk-away threshold). We propose shortening the window to 30 days (preferred), with 60 days as an acceptable fallback, and clarifying that the notice also operates as non-renewal notice. Separately noted but not flagged: there is no renewal reminder mechanic and no renewal price-uplift cap (fees here are transaction/revenue-share based under the Exhibits), which are rationale notes only under this rule.

proposal.comment: [Playbook] Section 4(c) only stops the Services and addresses Confidential Information, so we have added transition assistance and return of our data on exit. Our playbook requires up to six months of transition help at Kubient's then-current rates, return of our data in a machine-readable format within 30 days and certified deletion thereafter; we can accept 90 days of assistance if that is easier for Kubient.

ops.text: (v) at Customer's request, Kubient will provide reasonable transition assistance for up to six (6) months following expiration or termination at Kubient's then-current rates; (vi) within thirty (30) days of Customer's request, Kubient will return to Customer all Customer data then in Kubient's possession or control, including Requests, Content and all data collected, generated, maintained or stored by Kubient on Customer's behalf, in a commonly used, machine-readable format; and (vii) thereafter Kubient will delete such data from its systems and, upon request, certify such deletion to Customer in writing.

proposal.summary: Insert post-termination transition assistance and data return/deletion obligations into Section 4(c)

rationale: Section 4(c) is the only effects-of-termination provision and it addresses solely cessation of the Services, revocation of the licence, Customer's cessation of use and mutual return/destruction of Confidential Information. There is no transition-assistance, data return/export or certified-deletion obligation anywhere in the Agreement (no hits for transition, export, wind-down or machine-readable), even though Kubient collects, maintains and stores AP data and Requests on AP's behalf (Section 4(c)(iv), p0035). That falls short of both the preferred position (six months' assistance, 30-day machine-readable return, certified deletion) and the fallback (90 days' assistance, 30-day export), and the bare "return or destroy" option for Confidential Information risks the walk-away outcome of deletion without return. Inserted the model transition and data-return language into Section 4(c) as items (v)-(vii).
ruleTitle: Post-termination transition assistance and data return

quote: (ii) the Service will perform in all material respects to industry standards;
rationale: Section 9(b) contains a Kubient-given express performance warranty that meets or exceeds the preferred position: the Service will perform in all material respects to industry standards (p0034), services will comply with the Agreement and be free from errors that materially affect their utility (p0038), no viruses/Trojan Horses/worms or other malicious routines (p0036), and compliance with applicable Laws throughout the Term (p0037, p0041). Crucially, these warranties are not time-limited to 12 months/90 days — they run continuously for the Term, which is better for us than the preferred duration. The Section 13 disclaimer does not swallow the express warranty: it applies "Except as expressly set forth herein" and "except for the representations and warranties set forth in this Agreement," so the "as is" language cannot reach Section 9(b); this is not walk-away territory. Noted but not flagged: the Agreement does not spell out the model repair/replace/re-performance/refund remedy mechanic. That is not a material failure here because no clause makes any remedy exclusive or sole, so we retain our full contractual remedies (including damages, subject only to the mutual consequential-damages waiver in Section 7, and indemnification). Importing the model remedy sentence, which is exercisable "at Vendor's option," would in fact narrow our rights, so we should not propose it.

proposal.comment: [Playbook] We have added a standard insurance covenant, as Kubient hosts the Auction Platform and collects and stores visitor data on our behalf but the Agreement carries no insurance requirement. Our playbook position is CGL USD 1M/2M, E&O USD 2M and cyber USD 5M with certificates on request; we can work with E&O of USD 1M and cyber of USD 2M if needed.

ops.text: (j) Insurance. Kubient shall maintain, at its own expense, throughout the Term and for one (1) year thereafter: (i) commercial general liability insurance of not less than USD 1,000,000 per occurrence and USD 2,000,000 in the aggregate; (ii) professional liability (errors and omissions) insurance of not less than USD 2,000,000; (iii) cyber liability insurance of not less than USD 5,000,000 covering Kubient's collection, processing and storage of data hereunder; and (iv) workers' compensation insurance as required by applicable Law. Kubient shall provide Customer with certificates of insurance evidencing such coverage upon request.

proposal.summary: Insert vendor insurance covenant in General Provisions

rationale: The Agreement contains no insurance covenant anywhere (a full-text search for "insurance" returns nothing; the document is a single body section ending with General Provisions at p0063-p0073). Kubient hosts the Auction Platform and, per its warranty at p0035, collects, maintains, manages and stores visitor data, so it is a hosting/services vendor that processes Customer data. No insurance for such a vendor is walk-away territory under the rule, so this is a missing-clause deviation. We inserted a new General Provisions subsection (j) at the preferred limits (CGL USD 1M/2M, E&O USD 2M, cyber USD 5M, workers' compensation as required by law, certificates on request), noting the USD 1M E&O / USD 2M cyber fallback if Kubient pushes back.
